items.q: What's the fastest path Tilbury pitches for students aiming at $10K/month?
items.a: Become a **digital architect** — sell **high-value digital services** online — instead of the grades → university → job path that surveys put near **$5,473/month** for bachelor's graduates. The destination (**$10K/month**) matters more than which service vehicle you pick.

items.q: What is talent-maxxing and why does school get it wrong?
items.a: School trains weaknesses; Tilbury cites divergent thinking dropping from **98% genius-level at age five** to **2% by adulthood**. The **talent tree** has four types — **organizer, analyst, communicator, creative** — and the promise is only work where you have a clear advantage.

items.q: What three golden rules should a student service satisfy?
items.a: The service must **make a business more money**, **save time**, or **save money**. Example vehicles: brand identity, AI automation, deal-making, video editing, funnel creation — each mapped to talent types. Pick one and stick with it.

**Define → sell → deliver → fix → systemize.** Strip the offer to the simplest deliverable, sell before more learning (**99% rejections** are expected), let paying clients force skill, use AI to remove bottlenecks after a few deliveries, then systemize reliability (invoicing, follow-ups, due dates).

items.q: How does position-maxxing 10× the same skill?
items.a: Freelancers sell tasks ("I design logos," "I build chatbots"); digital architects sell **outcomes** — higher perceived value, **monthly savings**, traffic converted to customers. **Stop talking about what you do; talk about what it does for them.**

items.q: Why do people plateau at $10K without brand-maxxing?
items.a: Getting to **10K/month** and scaling to **20K–100K+** are different games. Casey Neistat sold to CNN for ~**$25M** largely on **personal brand**. Start with clean social profiles showing who you are and what you do before cold-messaging strangers who ignore empty profiles.

items.q: What happened when Mark's son followed the loop as an 18-year-old videographer?
items.a: He felt "not ready," sold **video editing** to a local caravan park, delivered under pressure, iterated with AI, systemized invoicing — and now earns **well over $10K/month**. Tilbury's line: **no better teacher than the real world.**

items.q: What beats raw talent once clients are paying?
items.a: **Reliability** — on-time delivery and clear communication — beats being the most talented. AI belongs **after** delivery experience to remove repetitive bottlenecks, not before the first sale.
